competitive_landscape: The water today is run by premium liveaboard phinisi and aluminium dive boats on 7–10 day circuits, plus chartered diesel speedboats and zodiacs for resort and dive-site transfers, with a minor public ASDP ferry on the Sorong↔Waisai run. The experience is rich underwater but rough on top: long open-water hauls, weather and tidal dependence, wet landings, and engine noise across protected reefs. That gap between a world-class destination and an undifferentiated, diesel-bound on-water experience is the opportunity — and a clean, fast, quiet network is the upgrade.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The all-electric core: intra-archipelago inter-resort transfers and dive-day arcs in the 10–40 nm band (Misool–Wayag–Waigeo–Kri), with Half-Foil and Shallow-Mode purpose-built for fringing-reef and atoll-pass geometry. Sorong↔Waisai at ~50 nm sits at the upper edge of all-electric range.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The dispersed Sorong-anchored network — Sorong↔Wayag ~95 nm, Sorong↔Misool ~110 nm, the Cenderawasih Bay whale-shark run ~280 nm, and the cross-archipelago link toward Ambon and the Banda Islands ~270–320 nm. Hybrid range with no charging-infrastructure dependency suits off-grid resort microgrids, and quiet-mode electric operation inside the no-take MPA is a clean-marine fit.

precedents.what: $100M, ~100-vessel phased electric-foiling network with JIH Global
precedents.why_it_matters: Proves a dispersed luxury-archipelago can adopt a clean-foiling network at scale — the playbook to replicate for Raja Ampat's resort and liveaboard flows.
A globally-rare private conservation precedent — the cleanest possible setting to lead with a zero-emission, low-wake fleet.

regulatory_note: Dual-gate Indonesian pathway: KKP (Ministry of Marine Affairs & Fisheries) governs the UNESCO MAB Biosphere and Misool MPA, while Kemenhub/DGST + BKI cover vessel class and transport. The conservation no-take zone and the IDR 1M visitor levy make a clean, low-wake, quiet-mode fleet a natural fit for the protected-waters mandate. Pertamina's Sorong marine bunker supports Quanta-LR diesel refuel.
seasonality: Inverted from much of Southeast Asia: the NW monsoon (Oct–Apr) is the 'wet-but-best-visibility' dive-tourism peak, while the SE monsoon (May–Sep) is drier but rougher, with the Cenderawasih whale-shark aggregation running May–Oct. Near-equatorial and effectively typhoon-free. Afternoon convective squalls and current-swept straits (Dampier) are exactly the chop and tide windows where foiling's smoother, faster ride becomes the premium.
signature_routes: Sorong ↔ Misool (south Raja Ampat resorts + no-take MPA) — Quanta-LR line-haul
Misool ↔ Wayag ↔ Kri ↔ Waigeo (intra-archipelago inter-resort mesh) — Pioneer II
summary: Raja Ampat is the ~1,500-island epicentre of the Coral Triangle off NW Papua — a UNESCO Man-and-the-Biosphere Reserve whose dive resorts and liveaboards draw a fast-growing premium-experience crowd (33,277 visitors in 2024). Guests fly into Sorong, then face a basin-class strait crossing to Waigeo, 100+ nm open-water hops to Misool and Wayag, and diesel speedboat or zodiac transfers between resorts. The on-water experience is the weakest link in an otherwise world-class trip — exactly where a smooth, quiet, foiling network changes everything, and the dispersed geography is squarely Quanta-LR range territory from the Sorong gateway.
tagline: The crown jewel of marine biodiversity — reached today by slow ferry, overnight liveaboard, and wet zodiac landings.

use_cases.body: Replace diesel speedboats and wet zodiac landings with a smooth, near-silent foiling transfer between Misool, Wayag, Waigeo and Kri — daily inter-resort hops and dive-day arcs in the 10–40 nm intra-archipelago band, with Half-Foil/Shallow-Mode handling the fringing-reef passes.
